subject.title: Session auto-recovery after restart loads full bloated context — paid 8 for 5 API calls

question: Should OpenClaw change its default compaction policy to bound active-session context before recovery, or keep the current opt-in maxActiveTranscriptBytes and truncateAfterCompaction controls?
rationale: Both paths affect existing-session cost, context retention, and startup behavior; source review shows existing controls but cannot establish that a new default is safe or desired.

options.title: Validate then tune the existing guard
options.body: Reproduce with effective configuration and improve the documented/default guard only if the restart path demonstrably bypasses it.

options.title: Keep opt-in policy
options.body: Retain current defaults and direct affected operators to configure the existing byte guard, transcript rotation, and a cheaper compaction model.

options.title: Adopt an explicit recovery default
options.body: Define and test a conservative default threshold that compacts before a resumed run, including an upgrade note and context-retention guarantees.

recommendation.title: Validate then tune the existing guard
recommendation.body: Reproduce with effective configuration and improve the documented/default guard only if the restart path demonstrably bypasses it.

likelyOwner.reason: Documented ownership associates this area with compaction and context-engine work.
